answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each claimed node to a Wesolowski VDF requiring a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each output serving as the sole input to the next. This dependency prevents GPUs from shortening an individual chain; simulating multiple clones requires proportionally many completed sequential chains. A public tide challenge, protocol kernel, and beacon-derived input prevent reuse, creating a strict physical time bottleneck for Sybil identities.
